summary: This section explains how the Tribunal makes and updates its decisions. It must listen to all sides before deciding and send a copy of the final order to everyone involved. The Tribunal can also fix clear mistakes in its orders within two years, as long as no appeal has been filed.
points: The Tribunal must give a reasonable chance to be heard to all parties before passing an order.
The Tribunal can pass any order it thinks is right after hearing the parties.
The Tribunal may fix any obvious mistake in its order within two years from the order date.
The Tribunal must fix a mistake if the parties bring it to its notice, within the two-year limit.
No mistake can be fixed if someone has already filed an appeal against that order.
The Tribunal must send a copy of every order to all parties concerned.
example: Meera Textiles Private Limited was involved in a dispute before the Tribunal. After giving both sides a fair chance to speak, the Tribunal issued its order and sent a copy to Meera Textiles and the other party. A month later, Meera Textiles noticed a clear typing error in the order regarding a name. Because no appeal had been filed yet, Meera Textiles pointed out the mistake to the Tribunal. Within the two-year time limit, the Tribunal corrected the mistake and updated the order to ensure accuracy.

terms.meaning: A specialized legal body set up to handle specific types of disputes and cases.
A formal request to a higher authority to change a lower decision.

watch: Remember that the Tribunal cannot fix mistakes in an order if an appeal has already been filed against it.
